limitations: Real macOS arm64 and Rosetta x86_64, temporary owned SQLite files, dedicated synthetic collector roots. Physical Intel was not exercised.
Seven interleaved samples per operation and row count; measured VACUUM and filesystem protection are included in the native action. Direction varies, so no overall latency improvement is claimed.

Fresh debug compilation initially hit ENOSPC; the original scratch resumed after space was freed; final linked XCTest completed. An initial x86 benchmark exhausted disk space and the isolated full run was repeated successfully. No production or external account profile was involved.
profileResets: No run used an existing user profile.

notes: Every comparison used independently generated synthetic schema18 files and the complete product public methods. Five mode/trigger/lock failures per executable were retried after removing the injected condition. Before-reset and after-crash state compare hash and count of every table and exact sorted app_metadata and exclusions. Only the wall-clock updated_at stamp of the freshly appended post-reset parsing_state row was checked for current-time range and normalized before cross-process comparison.

For crash injection, an owned slow SQLite trigger after earlier derived-table writes prolonged the uncommitted transaction. Each interruptible clear spilled more than 1 MiB of uncommitted WAL; a second reader separately saw epoch 7. For the after-commit case, a separate reader saw epoch 8 and an older read transaction still saw all seven events before SIGKILL. Restarted original, predecessor, and candidate retained the appropriate committed generation in every trial.
Apple Silicon and Rosetta cover SQLite actors; complete UI-model XCTest used Apple Silicon. No physical Intel, Windows, signed deployment or live account was involved.
